FE-A-0074.integrationProcedure: 1) Pick CRDT/OT stack. 2) Persist docs. 3) Add authz on rooms. 4) Test concurrent edits. 5) Plan compaction.

FE-A-0081.shortAnswer: Next.js App Router is a file-system router built around Server Components, nested layouts, and server-first data fetching by default.
FE-A-0081.answer: Answering “A Next.js application has good server response times but poor INP and occasional hydration mismatches. Build a debugging plan.?”: Next.js App Router is a file-system router built around Server Components, nested layouts, and server-first data fetching by default. Treating it like Pages Router (client everything) loses streaming, caching, and bundle benefits. Relevant ideas: app/ directory; layouts/templates; Server vs Client Components; loading.js/error.js; no client hooks in RSC; async server components. Place routes under app/, keep data fetching in Server Components, mark interactive islands with 'use client', and compose layouts that preserve state across navigations. Server defaults reduce JS but constrain browser APIs; overusing client components reintroduces waterfalls and large bundles.
FE-A-0081.integrationProcedure: 1) Migrate one route segment to app/. 2) Keep interactivity in leaf client components. 3) Use loading UI for suspense. 4) Verify RSC payload size. 5) Document client boundary rules.

FE-A-0082.shortAnswer: A design system packages reusable components, tokens, and guidelines so product UI stays consistent and accessible.
FE-A-0082.answer: Answering “Design a frontend platform for multiple teams sharing a design system, routing, authentication, observability, and deployment while avoiding both a monolith and unnecessary micro-frontends.?”: A design system packages reusable components, tokens, and guidelines so product UI stays consistent and accessible. Ad-hoc one-off UI creates drift, a11y gaps, and slow feature delivery. Relevant ideas: tokens; primitives/composites; accessibility contracts; versioning; runtime integration; shared deps risk. Publish tokens + components, document variants/states, enforce via lint/review, and version breaking changes. Heavy systems slow teams if rigid; too loose and they aren't systems. Start with tokens + few primitives.
FE-A-0082.integrationProcedure: 1) Extract tokens. 2) Build primitives. 3) Document states. 4) Adopt in one app. 5) Version releases.

FE-A-0083.shortAnswer: TanStack Query manages server state: caching, deduping, retries, stale-while-revalidate, and invalidation keyed by queryKey.
FE-A-0083.answer: Answering “Design a real-time collaborative editor frontend, including conflict handling, optimistic updates, offline behavior, and presence.?”: TanStack Query manages server state: caching, deduping, retries, stale-while-revalidate, and invalidation keyed by queryKey. Duplicating server cache in Redux/useState causes sync bugs and extra requests. Relevant ideas: queryKey; staleTime/gcTime; invalidation; mutations + optimistic UI; Cache-Control; ETag/conditional requests. Define stable keys, fetch in useQuery, invalidate on mutations, and tune staleTime so you don't refetch excessively. Great for remote data; bad for purely local UI state. Over-optimistic updates need rollbacks.
FE-A-0083.integrationProcedure: 1) Add QueryClientProvider. 2) Migrate GETs to useQuery. 3) Invalidate in mutations. 4) Set defaults for staleTime. 5) Devtools in staging.

FE-A-0084.shortAnswer: Flexbox lays out items along one main axis with alignment on the cross axis—ideal for toolbars, navs, and distributing space.
FE-A-0084.answer: Answering “Design a virtualized data grid supporting 100,000 rows, variable row heights, keyboard navigation, selection, sorting, filtering, and screen-reader usability.?”: Flexbox lays out items along one main axis with alignment on the cross axis—ideal for toolbars, navs, and distributing space. Mis-set flex-shrink/basis causes overflow or crushed content; nested flex without min-width:0 is a common trap. Relevant ideas: main/cross axis; grow/shrink/basis; justify/align; wrapping; grid-template-rows/columns; fr units and minmax. Set display:flex, choose direction, assign grow/shrink/basis intentionally, and use gap instead of margin hacks. Flex for 1D; Grid for 2D. Overusing flex for page grids creates deep nesting.
FE-A-0084.integrationProcedure: 1) Replace float/table hacks with flex for 1D UI. 2) Standardize gap tokens. 3) Fix overflow with min-size 0. 4) Document patterns.

FE-A-0085.shortAnswer: Identify the LCP element and shorten its critical path; reduce long tasks for INP; reserve space for images/fonts to limit CLS.
FE-A-0085.answer: Answering “How would you design frontend observability that connects user-visible failures to network requests, releases, traces, and feature flags without leaking sensitive data?”: Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) are Google's field metrics for loading, interactivity, and visual stability. Optimizing lab-only scores while ignoring field RUM leaves real users on slow devices/networks unhappy. Relevant ideas: LCP element; INP event delay; CLS layout shifts; field vs lab; mappings; private vs public maps. Identify the LCP element and shorten its critical path; reduce long tasks for INP; reserve space for images/fonts to limit CLS. Micro-optimizations that hurt UX (skeleton flicker) can improve scores incorrectly; prioritize user journeys. Use CrUX/RUM and Performance panel; correlate regressions with deploys and third-party scripts.
FE-A-0085.integrationProcedure: 1) Add RUM for CWV. 2) Fix top LCP resource. 3) Break long tasks. 4) Reserve media space. 5) Budget third parties.
